node.name: capture
node.description: transparent alias for the external `capture` CLI
node.whenToUse: you need to drive a real browser — screenshot, measure rendered geometry, capture a HAR or accessibility tree, or run JS against a live page.

passthrough.installHint: Install the Capture CLI: npm install -g @crouton-kit/capture

rootEntry.concept: browser automation for agents via the external Capture CLI (CDP screenshots, HAR, a11y, JS-exec, and site libs)
rootEntry.description: forwards verbatim to the external `capture` binary
rootEntry.whenToUse: a claim depends on what a real browser renders. When it depends on rendered geometry, clipping, overflow, stacking or nominal box intersection, computed style, or distance, read `crtr capture measure -h` — screenshots and accessibility trees orient but do not establish rendered structure. Capture attaches to any reachable CDP endpoint — a browser it launches, or the person's own CDP-enabled browser and its already-authenticated tabs (`--port <n>`, then `capture tab list`), so logged-in pages are in reach whenever that endpoint is exposed.

node.summary: transparent alias for the external `capture` CLI — every argument forwards verbatim
node.model: This branch owns no schema of its own: it execs `capture` with whatever args follow, inherits stdio, and propagates its exit code. Run `crtr capture -h` for capture's real command tree.
